issues.description: Field 'lectureName' has conflicting types between the problem statement UML and the reference implementation. In problem_statement.md the UML declares 'lectureName' as type int (line 64), while the solution implementation defines 'private String lectureName' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 6) and the textual example toString() in the problem statement formats lectureName as a String. This inconsistency can confuse students about the correct data type to use, the constructor signature order, and the expected behavior of getters/setters and toString().
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML/type annotation in problem_statement.md so that 'lectureName' is declared as a String (e.g. '-lectureName: String'). Also ensure any example output (toString) and textual descriptions consistently refer to lectureName as a String. This aligns the documentation with the solution and avoids confusion about the constructor and accessor signatures.
